newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary CIB sees foreigners buying 34 pct stake.
newsitem.headline: Hungary CIB sees foreigners buying 34 pct stake.

text.p: Three of the five foreign shareholders of Hungary's CIB Bank showed interest to use their pre-emption rights to buy the National Bank of Hungary's (NBH) 34 percent stake in the bank, CIB said on Friday.
"According to our knowledge, the foreign shareholders -- three of the five -- are considering to use their pre-emption rights," CIB Chairman and CEO Gyorgy Zdeborsky told a news conference.
He said the negotiations were likely to be completed by the end of September at the latest.

The five shareholders, each holding a stake of 13.2 percent, are Italy's Comit Holding International S.A., Germany's Bayerische Vereinsbank AG, Japan's Long-Term Credit Bank and Sakura Bank, and France's Societe Generale.
Zdeborsky said that CIB and its fully owned subsidiary CIB Hungaria were likely to hold shareholders meeting in July to vote on the merger of the banks on December 31.

He added that CIB Hungaria posted a pre-tax profit of 3.8 billion forints by the end of May, compared with the 5.5 billion forint target for whole 1997, and the two banks were likely to revise their year-end profit target up later this year. He declined the disclose what the target figure was.
He said the banks benefited from that the demand of Hungarian companies for loans had been increasing since the second half of last year.

CIB group is the largest lender to companies in Hungary, with its corporate loan portfolio totalling 150 billion to 160 billion forints at the end of May, compared with the two banks' combined balance sheet total of between 330 and 340 billion forints, Zdeborsky said.
CIB officials said the bank began expansion in managing investment funds.
Investment notes of the CIB-Kincsem Fund, worth some 1.2 billion forints were subscribed earlier this week and the group plans to release a new fund later in the year.
